title: Evaluation of the scalar-restriction inverse mate
statement: Let CE and CF be towers of commutative rings on schemes X and Y, f : X → Y, and n a coefficient level. Let rX and rY be maps of their sequence ring sheaves, and aX and aY their level-n coefficient maps. Assume the level maps commute with the canonical inverse-image coefficient identifications. Suppose normalized scalar-restriction/pushforward and scalar-restriction/evaluation isomorphisms d, eX, eY act as identity on all underlying sections. Then level-n evaluation of the component at any CF-system M on Y of the inverse adjunction mate of d.inv is an isomorphism. No flatness assumption is needed. The systems, pushforward, and adjunctions are those of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting], evaluation is [def-sp-varying-ring-operations], and scalar restriction is [def-coef-semilinear-system-models].

source.place: Tag 03EK; agent-formulated normalized evaluation and mate-cube substep of blueprint sk-thm-purity-transport Step 10, for the existing whole-system scalar-restriction/pullback comparison.

proof.text: Use the canonical pushforward/evaluation isomorphisms. Their inverse mates are inverses of the canonical pullback/evaluation isomorphisms by the unit normalization and injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalence.

The square formed by d.inv, the canonical pushforward/evaluation comparisons, eX, eY, and the fixed-ring scalar direct-image comparison commutes: each of its six component maps is identity on the same underlying additive sections. Transport the carrier equalities, compose the identities and apply module-sheaf extensionality.

Apply injectivity of the mate equivalence and its composition/whiskering laws to obtain the corresponding inverse-image cube. The fixed-ring scalar inverse mate is invertible. All other cube edges are evaluation or restriction isomorphisms, so cancel those edges to prove invertibility of the evaluated whole-system inverse mate.

proof_origin: K1 agent-written proof of the evaluation substep. Fully proved in Lean; abstract towers keep coefficient quotient constructions out of categorical elaboration.

theorem restriction_inverse_mate_eval_isIso
    (CE CF : ℕ → CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (τE : ∀ n, CE (n + 1) ⟶ CE n) (τF : ∀ n, CF (n + 1) ⟶ CF n)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ)
    (rX : SemilinearProperOpen.ringSystem CE τE X ⟶
      SemilinearProperOpen.ringSystem CF τF X)
    (rY : SemilinearProperOpen.ringSystem CE τE Y ⟶
      SemilinearProperOpen.ringSystem CF τF Y)
    (aX : VaryingRing.coefficients CE X n ⟶ VaryingRing.coefficients CF X n)
    (aY : VaryingRing.coefficients CE Y n ⟶ VaryingRing.coefficients CF Y n)
    (hs : (StrictTower.constantRingIso (CE n) f).hom ≫ aX =
      (proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map aY ≫
        (StrictTower.constantRingIso (CF n) f).hom)
    (d : SemilinearSections.res rX ⋙ SemilinearProperOpen.push CE τE f ≅
      SemilinearProperOpen.push CF τF f ⋙ SemilinearSections.res rY)
    (hd : ∀ (N : VaryingRing.Modules CF τF X) (U : (ℕ × Y.ProEt)ᵒᵖ)
      (x : ((SemilinearSections.res rX ⋙ SemilinearProperOpen.push CE τE f).obj N).val.obj U),
      HEq ((d.hom.app N).val.app U x) x)
    (eX : SemilinearSections.res rX ⋙ VaryingRing.eval CE τE X n ≅
      VaryingRing.eval CF τF X n ⋙ SemilinearSections.res aX)
    (heX : ∀ (N : VaryingRing.Modules CF τF X) (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ),
      HEq (fun x ↦ (eX.hom.app N).val.app U x)
        (fun x : N.val.obj (op (n, U.unop)) ↦ x))
    (eY : SemilinearSections.res rY ⋙ VaryingRing.eval CE τE Y n ≅
      VaryingRing.eval CF τF Y n ⋙ SemilinearSections.res aY)
    (heY : ∀ (N : VaryingRing.Modules CF τF Y) (U : Y.ProEtᵒᵖ),
      HEq (fun x ↦ (eY.hom.app N).val.app U x)
        (fun x : N.val.obj (op (n, U.unop)) ↦ x))
    (M : VaryingRing.Modules CF τF Y) :
    IsIso ((VaryingRing.eval CE τE X n).map
      ((((mateEquiv (SemilinearProperOpen.ordinaryAdj CF τF f)
        (SemilinearProperOpen.ordinaryAdj CE τE f)).symm
          (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ d.inv)).natTrans).app M))
